pageReviews.content: Front cover: Pokémon Trading Card Game Advanced Rulebook, Version 1.
Inside-front artwork and numbered page 1 table of contents.
Advanced rules: scope, win conditions, deck size, setup, Pokémon Powers, Stage 2 evolution, Weakness, Resistance, and attack ordering.
Attack ordering continued; Sleep, Confusion, Paralysis, Poison, condition replacement, and after-turn processing.
Complete Rules Reference: required materials, game model, win conditions, starting hands, Bench, Prizes, and setup.
Cards in play and anatomy of Pokémon, Trainer, and Energy cards.
Turn sequence, drawing, playing Basic Pokémon, and evolution restrictions.
Attaching Energy, playing Trainers, retreating, and using Pokémon Powers.
Attack declaration, Energy requirements, Colorless requirements, Weakness, Resistance, and damage counters.
Knock Outs, Prizes, Active replacement, turn completion, and Sleep and Confusion reference.
Paralysis, Poison, combined conditions, followed by the product-level promotional insert occupying page position 19.
Deck construction and Expert Rules for what counts as an attack and attack resolution order.
Damage calculation, retreat with Double Energy, short draws and searches, and simultaneous opening mulligans.
Simultaneous wins, Sudden Death, and glossary through Hit Points.
Questions/contact page and credits with 1999–2000 copyright markings.
Back-cover Pokémon Trading Card Game League promotional insert.

rulings.clarification: Strikes Back applies when Machamp is damaged on the Bench by an attack.

rulings.clarification: An eligible Active Ditto transforms automatically rather than optionally.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Powers > TRANSFORM; 1-20-00 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: After the opposing Active is Knocked Out, Ditto copies the replacement Active without an intervening unopposed state.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Powers > TRANSFORM; Feb 17 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: A Ditto copying Blastoise must still satisfy Rain Dance’s printed Water Energy and Water Pokémon requirements.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Attacks > AGILITY; Jan 27 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: A successful Agility effect prevents Moltres’s Wildfire attack effect against that Pokémon.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Attacks > CONVERSION 1/2; Jan 20 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Conversion remains on the affected Pokémon if Porygon retreats or leaves play; it ends through the affected Pokémon’s normal effect-clearing transitions.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Attacks > CONVERSION 1/2; Feb 10 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Conversion ends when the affected opposing Pokémon goes to the Bench, not when Porygon does.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Attacks > SUPER FANG; Feb 17 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Resolve Super Fang’s half-remaining-HP damage, then apply PlusPower.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Pokémon Attacks > SWORDS DANCE; Jan 20 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Swords Dance’s effect ends when Scyther goes to the Bench.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > CLEFAIRY DOLL / MYSTERIOUS FOSSIL; Feb 10 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Mysterious Fossil is a Trainer card in hand and does not satisfy the opening Basic Pokémon requirement.

rulings.topic: Clefairy Doll and Mysterious Fossil Knock Out

rulings.clarification: Knocking Out Clefairy Doll or Mysterious Fossil does not award a Prize.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > DEFENDER; Feb 10 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Defender can reduce damage an attached Pokémon’s own attack does to itself.

rulings.topic: Super Energy Removal and Double Colorless
rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > ENERGY REMOVAL / SUPER ENERGY REMOVAL; Feb 10 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Super Energy Removal discards Energy cards, so two Double Colorless Energy cards are two removable cards.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > PLUSPOWER; Feb 17 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: PlusPower does not create damage when the attack’s damage is reduced to zero before PlusPower applies.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > PLUSPOWER; Feb 3 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: PlusPower is added before Invisible Wall evaluates the attack’s damage total.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > POTION / SUPER POTION; Feb 3 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: A damage counter in printed card text represents 10 damage.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Trainer Cards > SWITCH; Feb 3 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Switch can move an Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed Active Pokémon.

rulings.sourceCitation: Compendium > Energy Cards > ENERGY CARDS IN GENERAL; 2-10-00 WotC Chat
rulings.clarification: Double Colorless Energy is one Energy card attachment and does not permit another Energy-card attachment that turn.

currentEntries.approvalRationale: A reenactor is a literal stand-in and the shield-bearing illustration preserves the decoy/sacrificial-body relationship.
The eerie elderly regular is a legible mysterious old fossil while preserving the existing stand-in-Basic structure.
The metal-detectorist literally recovers a buried old item, matching recovery of a Trainer from the discard pile.
The chauffeur and open car visibly move someone; the current zero-retreat presentation and vintage switch share mobility.
The scout selects a performer; both the current and vintage effects exchange or find a selected Pokémon.
The circular road depicts cycling cards back around, preserving the current pay-cards-to-draw-one concept.
The current primary action is already exactly draw 2; the doorstep parcel supplies a delivery metaphor.
The illustration and current effect both hinge on an optimistic coin flip that recovers a discarded resource.
The matchmaker introduces a candidate; both effects move an opponent’s Basic Pokémon onto the Bench.
The Guv’nor visibly controls an Energy token and the current effect already removes opposing Energy.
The illustration checks a fan of cards and ejects a patron, preserving hand inspection and removal.
The illustration treats an injury and both current and vintage effects heal 20 damage.
The hazard-control presentation is the approved closest fit for clearing harmful conditions.
The bouncer physically blocks harm and both effects reduce incoming attack damage.

Your opponent shuffles his or her hand into his or her deck, then draws 7 cards.
Discard 2 of the other cards from your hand in order to put a Trainer card from your discard pile into your hand.
You and your opponent show each other your hands, then shuffle all the Trainer cards from your hands into your decks.

Trade 1 of the other cards in your hand for up to 2 basic Energy cards from your discard pile.
Your Active Pokémon is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned.

Remove all damage counters from all of your own Pokémon with damage counters on them, then discard all Energy cards attached to those Pokémon.
Choose 1 Basic Pokémon card from your opponent's discard pile and put it onto his or her Bench. (You can't play Pokémon Flute if your opponent's Bench is full.)
Look at up to 5 cards from the top of your deck and rearrange them as you like.
Discard your hand, then draw 7 cards.

Search your deck for a basic Energy card and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward.

newPresentations.illustrationConcept: A regular gives up two blank betting slips at a crowded pub table; two locals point him to the single wanted item in an overfilled lost-property cabinet.
A dressed-up regular loses the outer layers of a grand makeover under a bracing cold shower, returning to an earlier self.
A smug bogus expert sweeps an opponent’s whole hand together, shuffles it, and deals seven fresh blank cards.
A fresh-faced newcomer with a VIP wristband is ushered past the middle velvet-rope checkpoint straight to the final tier.
A last train collects one regular while their attached clutter is left behind on the platform.
A bartender surrenders one drink from their own side to remove two drinks from a rival patron.
One unwanted item is traded across the bar for up to two recovered drinks from the empties tray.
A bartender places a small extra measure beside the active regular for one immediate burst of force.
A waiting room treats every injured member of one group while their remaining drinks are collected for disposal.
A focused punter studies and deliberately rearranges five race cards before the next draw.
A quizmaster bins a team’s current answer sheet and hands them seven clean slips.
A first aider restores a fallen novice to the bench, clearly alive but still carrying half their injuries.
A substantial breakfast restores a larger amount of strength after one attached drink is given up.
A seated reserve is beckoned off the bench and made to take the active darts oche while the former player steps aside.
A punter flips a coin while reaching into a lucky-dip barrel and pulls out one chosen local’s portrait token from many.
An older regular helps one benched patron, coat and bags together into a waiting cab home.
A bartender reaches into a mixed cellar crate and retrieves the one charged Energy token needed for a refill.
A player feeds their whole hand into a fruit machine; one coin flip pays either eight cards or only one.
